v1/Atlas/TheoryOfComputation/report.json.withdrawn: Confirmed against Probabilistic.lean:153 and :296. InBPPWithError is `∃ (Q : Type) (_ : DecidableEq Q) (M : PTM Q Γ) ...` with no Fintype Q, and the PTM structure (BPP.lean:20) does not restrict Q either. P and NP do require it (Complexity.lean:81,86: `∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Fintype Q) ...`). I checked that the loosening is material with a construction that fits the actual fields. Take Γ = Option Bool with blank = none and inputAlpha = {some 0, some 1}. Take Q = List Bool ⊕ Bool with q₀ = inl [], qAccept = inr true and qReject = inr false. Let δ₀ = δ₁ append each bit read to the state and move right. On reading none, δ moves to inr (classical membership of the stored prefix in HALT). With t' n = n+1, which is IsBigO n^1, this decides the undecidable language {w : prefix before first blank ∈ HALT} with error 0. So 'poly-time PTM' in the Lean is not the textbook object, and the lemma is a statement about a different, much larger class. The lemma probably stays true for that class, so the defect sits in the definition, but the needs-lean-change fix (add Fintype Q) is correct. Side points also check out: the 2^{-poly(n)} strengthening is the separate, sorry'd amplification_lemma_exp; the proof rests on the sorry'd one_step_majority_vote; and the extra 0 < ε₁ hypothesis is harmless.

v1/Atlas/TheoryOfComputation/report.json.statement: Let $F$ be a finite field with $|F| \geq 3m$, and let $B_1, B_2$ be branching programs on the Boolean variables $x_1, \dots, x_m$. For $i = 1, 2$ let $p_i \in F[x_1, \dots, x_m]$ be the multilinear extension of the Boolean function computed by $B_i$ (for a read-once branching program this is its arithmetization), and let $r$ be chosen uniformly at random from $F^m$. (1) If $B_1 \equiv B_2$, that is, $B_1$ and $B_2$ compute the same Boolean function, then $\Pr[p_1(r) = p_2(r)] = 1$. (2) If $B_1 \not\equiv B_2$, then $\Pr[p_1(r) = p_2(r)] \leq 1/3$.
v1/Atlas/TheoryOfComputation/report.json.title: Claim (Agreement probability of arithmetized branching programs)

v1/Atlas/TheoryOfComputation/report.json.withdrawn: Checked against InteractiveProofs.lean:19-95. Verifier (line 26) is a bare structure of two arbitrary functions, sendMessage and decide. Nothing bounds time or computability. InIP only requires t = O(n^k) and r = O(n^j) (IsBigO, Complexity.lean:76: ∃ c n₀, 0<c ∧ ∀ n≥n₀, f n ≤ c·g n). Witness for any A: Q := Unit (it has DecidableEq), V := ⟨fun _ _ _ _ => [], fun w _ _ _ => @decide (w ∈ A) (Classical.dec _)⟩, P := fun _ _ => [], k = j = 0, t = r = fun _ => 0. IsBigO 0 (n^0) holds with c = 1. With n = 0 coins, Finset.univ over Fin 0 → Bool has exactly one element, so numAccepting is 1 or 0 depending on w ∈ A, whatever the prover, and acceptProb = that / 2^0. That gives completeness (1 ≥ 2/3) and soundness (0 ≤ 1/3) for every prover P'. So InIP holds for every language. The source requires a probabilistic polynomial-time verifier, which the Lean drops, so needs-lean-change is right.

The declaration at NPCompleteness.lean:115 is `∀ A, InNP A → PolyReducible A B`, with `open TuringMachine`. No other PolyReducible definition exists that could shadow it, so it uses the defective TuringMachine.PolyReducible confirmed in the PolyTimeReducible claim. The defect changes which languages count as NP-hard. Take Γ with distinct symbols a, b and a blank, and let B = {a a :: x | x ∈ SAT′} for an NP-complete SAT′. B is NP-hard in Sipser's sense. But A = {[b,b]}, a finite set and so in NP, has no Lean reduction to B. Under the Lean definition, f([b,b]) must be a prefix of [b,b] padded with blanks, or, when k = 0, a prefix of that string with its first cell overwritten in one step. Either way its second symbol is b ≠ a, so f([b,b]) ∉ B. Conversely, with uncomputable reductions allowed, B = {v | v ≠ []} (a language in P) is NP-hard in Lean unconditionally, whereas in Sipser's sense it is NP-hard only if P = NP. So Lean's IsNPHard is not the textbook notion. The article matches the Lean text, so status_ok = true and needs-lean-change, with the fix belonging upstream in IsPolyTimeComputableFunction, are correct.

Checked against InteractiveProofs.lean:26-95. Verifier is a structure with two fields, sendMessage and decide. Both are arbitrary functions of (w, n, coins, transcript), with no computability or time bound. InIP only asks for polynomial bounds (IsBigO, Complexity.lean:76) on the coin count t and the round count r. The counterexample works for any language A. Take Q := Unit, V.decide := fun w _ _ _ => @decide (w ∈ A) (Classical.dec _), any sendMessage and any prover, t = r = fun _ => 0, and k = j = 0. IsBigO (fun _ => 0) (fun n => n^0) holds with c = 1, n₀ = 0. With n = 0 coins, Fin 0 → Bool has exactly one element and 2^0 = 1. So acceptProb is 1 when w ∈ A (at least 2/3) and 0 when w ∉ A (at most 1/3, for every prover). Every language is therefore in InIP, and ISO_bar_in_IP is vacuous. Sipser's IP requires V to be a probabilistic polynomial-time TM, so this needs a Lean change. The theorem's own proof uses the same trick: defaultGraphPermuter (GraphNonIsoIP.lean:51-68) decides ISO membership classically.

InIP A holds for every A (see the InIP entry, construction checked against the Verifier fields). So ip_eq_pspace (InteractiveProofs.lean:161) says every language over every Γ is in PSPACE. InPSPACE (SpaceComplexity.lean:153) means InSPACE (n^k): some TM over a Fintype state type Q has M.language = A and TMRunsInSpace, which includes isDecider. For Γ = Bool, a TM with finite Q is determined by finite data up to relabeling states, so only countably many languages are in PSPACE. Uncountably many languages are subsets of List Bool. So IP_subset_PSPACE is false and the theorem is false as stated; it rests on sorry. The root cause is in InIP, so needs-lean-change on InIP is right, and the theorem statement can stay once InIP is fixed.

Checked CFGtoPDA.lean:21 and :941. IsPDARecognizable A is `∃ (σ γ : Type u_pda) (P : PDA T σ γ), P.language = A`, and the PDA has no finiteness requirement. The same List-state PDA (σ = List T, γ = PUnit.{u_pda+1}, accept = A) shows IsPDARecognizable A for every A. So the IsContextFree hypothesis does no work, and the statement doesn't capture the textbook claim (a finite-state, finite-stack PDA). Also confirmed that QState has the constructor `pushing : List (Symbol T N) → QState T N`, so even toPDA g is infinite-state. The proof itself has no sorry, but the statement is trivial. needs-lean-change is justified.

Checked CFGPDAEquiv.lean:21, PDA (ContextFree.lean:517: just step, start, accept; no finiteness on σ or γ), Step/Reaches/Accepts/language, and pda_language_isContextFree (CFLInterRegular.lean:17), which is `sorry`. The counterexample typechecks. Take σ = List α : Type u and γ = PUnit (also Type u), with step q (some a) none = {(q ++ [a], none)}, all other steps ∅, start = [], accept = A. Step.mk with pop = push = none takes (q, a::input, s) to (q++[a], input, s). Reachable configs from ([], w, []) keep the invariant state ++ input = w with an empty stack, so the language is exactly A. Over any nonempty α there are non-context-free languages (e.g. unary {a^(n²)}), so the ← direction is false. The theorem only compiles because of the sorry'd lemma.

TuringEnumerator (line 226) is {toTM : TM Q Γ, prints : Config Q Γ → Set (List Γ)}, with prints unconstrained, and language = {w | ∃ n, w ∈ prints (run n)}. For any A over a nonempty Γ (pick b : Γ), take Q = Bool, blank = b, inputAlpha = ∅, qAccept = true, qReject = false, any q₀ and δ, and prints := fun _ => A. Then E.language = A, so every A is Turing-enumerable. For Γ = Bool, A = {[]} is not recognizable: initConfig [] = initConfig [M.blank] pointwise, so [] ∈ L(M) → [M.blank] ∈ L(M). The right-to-left direction (isTuringRecognizable_of_isTuringEnumerable, proved by sorry at line 330) is therefore false, and so is the iff stated for all Γ. needs-lean-change is right.

v1/Atlas/TheoryOfComputation/report.json.withdrawn: The TM structure (line 30) puts no finiteness on Q or Γ, but Sipser's 7-tuple (the cited source) has finite Q, Σ, Γ. I checked that their construction typechecks against the real fields. Take Γ = Option Bool, blank = none, inputAlpha = {some true, some false} (so blank_not_in_inputAlpha holds), Q = List Bool ⊕ Bool (DecidableEq derivable), q₀ = inl [], qAccept = inr true, qReject = inr false (distinct). Let δ (inl l) (some b) = (inl (l++[b]), some b, R) and δ (inl l) none = (if l ∈ S then inr true else inr false, none, R), defined classically. This machine halts on every input and accepts exactly the words whose prefix before the first blank lies in an arbitrary S, so noncomputable languages become decidable. inputAlpha is also never used by initConfig, language or isDecider. This is a material departure from the textbook model, so the needs-lean-change call is right. Part of the remedy is in TM.language/isDecider, not the structure itself, but the missing finiteness is a defect of the structure on its own.

IsTuringRecognizable (line 139) is ∃ Q, DecidableEq Q, M : TM Q Γ, M.language = A, where TM.language = {w : List Γ | M.accepts w} ranges over all of List Γ. initConfig w = initConfig (w ++ [M.blank]) by funext: positions < |w| agree, and position |w| is M.blank in both. So every recognizable A has w ∈ A ↔ w ++ [M.blank] ∈ A for some blank in Γ. For example, {[]} over Bool is not recognizable, while it is recognizable in Sipser's sense. Infinite Q also makes noncomputable languages recognizable, using the construction checked for the TM node. The defined class differs materially from the textbook's, so needs-lean-change is right.

IsTuringDecidable (line 144) adds M.isDecider (∀ w : List Γ, M.halts w) to the same TM.language. The blank-closure argument (initConfig w = initConfig (w ++ [M.blank])) applies unchanged. No nonempty language that is never closed under appending a symbol is decidable, e.g. {[]} over Bool or lang_akbk. The infinite-state construction I checked for the TM node halts on every input, so it makes arbitrary, noncomputable prefix-defined languages decidable. This differs materially from Sipser's class, so needs-lean-change is right.

In Lean, prints is an arbitrary field of type Config Q Γ → Set (List Γ), not determined by δ, the states or the tape. The run from the all-blank initConfig only chooses which configurations prints is evaluated at. With prints := fun _ => A, every A ⊆ List Γ (Γ nonempty) is L(E) for some enumerator; I checked that the TM fields can be filled: Q = Bool, qAccept ≠ qReject, inputAlpha = ∅. The article's notion of a TM that itself prints strings becomes vacuous, and that makes the Lecture 6 equivalence false. This is a material departure from the source, so needs-lean-change is right.

v1/Atlas/TheoryOfComputation/report.json.withdrawn: HALT_TM_not_decidable (Decidability.lean:429) assumes `enc : TMEncoding Γ`, which is TuringMachine.TMEncoding. That type is empty: universalSim's TM gives a blank, and Q := Set (List Γ) in TMDesc with q₀ := S, qAccept := ∅, qReject := univ makes S ↦ encode(desc S) an injection Set (List Γ) → List Γ, contradicting Cantor. The proof itself is sorry-free (A_TM_not_decidable at line 311 and A_TM_decidable_of_HALT_TM_decidable have no sorry). But a statement whose hypothesis can never be met proves nothing about the halting problem. The article's frontmatter says `statement: formalized` and `proof: formalized`, which overstates what Lean establishes. Both status_ok false and needs-lean-change are right.

Checked SelfReference.lean:54-58 and 375-444. TMEncoding has the fields printTMDesc_spec (printTMDesc w halts with w on the tape on every input) and q_computable (IsComputableFunction (fun w => encode (printTMDesc w))). The proof of computable_q_is_computable is literally ⟨fun w => enc.encode (enc.printTMDesc w), enc.q_computable, ⟨enc.printTMDesc w, rfl, enc.printTMDesc_spec w⟩⟩, a repackaging of the hypothesis. encode has no injectivity requirement. The only instance, concreteTMEncoding (line 389), sets encode := desc.source and source := w, so q is the identity and ⟨P_w⟩ is w itself rather than a description of a machine. The real content of the lemma, that w ↦ ⟨P_w⟩ is TM-computable for a genuine encoding, is never proved. needs-lean-change is justified.

Confirmed against RecursionTheorem.lean:63. The declaration states `∀ computable t : TMIndex → TMIndex, ∃ R, ∀ w, behavior R w = behavior (t R) w`, which is the fixed-point form. The article (and v1 description) states Sipser's form: for every TM T there is R with R(w) behaving as T(⟨w, R⟩). The objects differ (a computable index map versus a machine T), and so do the conclusions. I grepped RecursionTheorem.lean, SelfReference.lean, FixedPointTheorem.lean and TMCodingInstance.lean, and no declaration states the textbook form; SelfReference.recursion_theorem is also the language-level fixed-point form. The auditor's derivation is correct against the TMCoding fields: take t = C.smn T, so ht = C.isComputable_smn_apply T. Then recursion_theorem gives R with behavior R w = behavior (smn T R) w, and C.smn_spec T R w rewrites the right side to behavior T (pair w (encode R)). The Lean result is not wrong; it implies the textbook form in one step. Still, readback is not exact, and a v1 override cannot change the textbook statement, so adding the corollary declaration and pointing the article at it is the appropriate fix.

v1/Atlas/TheoryOfComputation/report.json.withdrawn: Checked SelfReference.lean:177-203 and 522-534. TMCoding.recognizable_enumSearch_computable says: for any P, if {encode M | P M} is Turing-recognizable, then every t with P(t M) and |encode M| < |encode (t M)| satisfies IsComputable t. The proof applies this with P = IsMinimalIndex to the t it obtains by choice, then calls the recursion theorem. That axiom is the central textbook step (an enumerator for MIN_TM yields a computable search for a longer minimal machine), so the key step is assumed. Take a genuine coding with genuine computability and P := fun _ => True. The set of all valid codes is recognizable, but uncountably many length-increasing t exist and only countably many are computable, so the axiom is false there. languages_beyond_length is also assumed. The edge mismatch also holds: article 047 has lean: SelfReference.MIN_TM, which is defined over SelfReference.TMEncoding, while this theorem uses TuringMachine.MIN_TM_Coding over TMCoding. I did not verify the auditor's hedged 'likely vacuous' remark, that TMCoding may have no instances. The main defect stands without it.

Checked SelfReference.lean:638-706 and Decidability.lean:47-100. The conclusion of true_but_unprovable_statement is ∃ d : TMDesc Γ, ¬d.accepts ∧ enc.encode d ∉ provable. That is token-for-token the conclusion of godel_first_incompleteness; the only change is that the recognizability hypothesis becomes an explicit TM P with P.language = provable. The witness comes from enc.selfRef P inside the proof, and its defining property is d.accepts ↔ P accepts ⟨d⟩. That property, the identification of d with Sipser's R, and the input 0 (TMDesc carries an arbitrary input) never appear in the statement. The article asserts (1) and (2) about one specific statement φ_U = ⟨R,0⟩ ∈ the complement of A_TM, and the Lean only gives an existential. So the article implies the Lean statement but not the other way round, a material weakening. needs-lean-change is justified.

Checked v1/Atlas/TheoryOfComputation/code/RegularLanguages.lean:22: `abbrev FiniteAutomaton (α σ : Type*) := DFA α σ` adds no Fintype/Finite constraint on σ or α. The file shows that Mathlib's DFA (fields step : σ → α → σ, start, accept : Set σ) has no built-in finiteness. regular_union (lines 53-57) pulls a separate Fintype σ witness out of Language.IsRegular and supplies `inferInstance` for σ₁ × σ₂, and DFA.pumping_lemma' (line 225) takes [Fintype σ] as an extra hypothesis on M : DFA α σ. So finiteness of states is imposed only where the definition is used, and the alphabet's finiteness is never required. The article and Sipser require Q and Σ finite, so the docstring's 'exactly the data packaged by Mathlib's DFA' overclaims. Since the v1 textbook statement must not be edited, needs-lean-change (add finiteness or correct the docstring) is the right fix kind. status_ok true is consistent (a definition, nothing to prove). Caveat: there is no local Mathlib checkout, so the DFA structure was not read in Mathlib's source; I relied on the file's usage and Mathlib's standard DFA definition.

Confirmed: the Lean statement is false. inP_of_polyTimeReducible applies inP_of_polyReducible_inP, which rests on the sorry'd inP_preimage_of_isPolyTimeComputableFunction. Counterexample over Γ = Bool, writing b for a fixed blank and a ≠ b. (1) B = {v | v ≠ [] ∧ v₀ ≠ b} is in P. A 3-state TM whose δ in q₀ goes to qReject on reading b and to qAccept otherwise decides B. It halts after one step on every input, so runsInTime (fun _ => 1), and IsBigO (fun _ => 1) (fun n => n^0) holds with c = 1. (2) For any A ⊆ {a :: u}, set f w = [a] if w ∈ A and [] otherwise. f satisfies IsPolyTimeComputableFunction through the immediately halting TM (q₀ = qAccept), as in the PolyTimeReducible claim, and w ∈ A ↔ f w ∈ B. (3) The theorem would then put every such A in P. But InP needs a TM with a Fintype state set over the finite Γ = Bool, which gives only countably many languages up to relabeling the states, while there are uncomputably many such A. Taking A undecidable gives a contradiction just as well. So the sorry'd lemma is unprovable and the theorem is false as stated. The status (statement only, no proof) is consistent.

Checked against the source. PolyTimeReducible unfolds to TuringMachine.PolyReducible (Complexity.lean:113), which uses IsPolyTimeComputableFunction (Complexity.lean:104). That definition asks only that `n ≤ |w|^k`, that `F.isHaltConfig (F.runOnInput w n)` holds, and that `Config.readTape (F.runOnInput w n) (f w).length = f w`. readTape (Reductions.lean:17) reads only the first |f w| cells and puts no condition on later cells. Counterexample: take Q = Bool, q₀ = qAccept = true, qReject = false, inputAlpha = ∅, any blank and δ. This satisfies every TM field, including blank_not_in_inputAlpha and qReject_ne_qAccept. Then runOnInput w 0 = initConfig w is halting, 0 ≤ |w|^k holds, and readTape(initConfig w) m gives the length-m prefix of w followed by blanks. So any f with f w ∈ {[], take 1 w}, chosen per w and possibly uncomputably, counts as polynomial-time computable. The no-constant bound point is also right. For k ≥ 1 the empty input forces n ≤ 0^k = 0, so q₀ must already be a halting state and the machine halts at step 0 on every input. For k = 0 at most one step is allowed. So the relation lets uncomputable reductions through and excludes genuine ones, which is not Sipser's ≤_P. The same unconstrained output length is present in IsComputableFunction (Reductions.lean:23). needs-lean-change is justified.

Checked Clique.lean:262–356, InP/InTIME (Complexity.lean) and TM, initConfig and decides (TuringMachines.lean). InP needs a TM M with M.decides CLIQUEEnc, which ranges over all w : List SATCliqueSymbol. Let b = M.blank (whatever symbol that is). TM.initConfig [clique []] and initConfig [clique [], b] are the same function: cell 1 is blank either way. So the machine accepts both or neither. [clique []] ∈ CLIQUEEnc, because HasKClique (reductionGraph []) 0 holds with s = ∅ (the vertex type is Fin 0 × Fin 3). [clique [], b] has length 2, so it is not in CLIQUEEnc. So no TM decides CLIQUEEnc, the hypothesis InP CLIQUEEnc is unsatisfiable, and the theorem is vacuous. The readback findings also hold. CLIQUEEnc only contains reduction-image instances, uses single-symbol encodings over an infinite alphabet, and is a different object from Clique.CLIQUE. The proof also relies on threeSATToCliqueEnc_polyTime, which is `sorry`.

Checked Tableau.lean:28-109 and NondeterministicTM.lean:43. NTM.initConfig has state q₀, headPos 0, and w on the tape. encodeConfigRow puts inl state at column headPos and inr (tape j) elsewhere, so row 0 is [inl q₀, inr w1, inr w2, ...]: the scanned symbol w0 is overwritten. Counterexample for |w| = n ≥ 2: k = 1 (size_pos holds); every row is encodeConfigRow (initConfig w) n except that row n-1, column 0 is inl qAccept. Row n-1 ≠ row 0 because n ≥ 2, so start holds, and accept holds with j = 0. move ranges over top rows i ≤ n-2, which all equal the initial row, and columns 1 ≤ j ≤ n-2. At j = 1, a = inl q₀, so the premise of the no-head clause fails, and b = inr _, so the head clause (∀ q γ, b = inl q → …) is vacuous. At j ≥ 2, a, b and c are all inr, so e = b is required. The bottom row agrees with the initial row at columns ≥ 1, so e = b holds, and the head clause is again vacuous. For n = 2 there are no interior columns. So Tableau M w is inhabited for every NTM M and every w with |w| ≥ 2. That includes an NTM with q₀ = qReject, which never accepts, so accepts_from_tableau (NPCompleteness.lean:153, sorry) is false. The structure does not capture Sipser's accepting computation history, and the needs-lean-change fix is warranted. status_ok true is consistent with the frontmatter rule (no sorry in the structure, v1 passed).

The defect is real, but the auditor's account of what it does, and the proposed fix, are incomplete. IsPolyTimeComputableFunction (Complexity.lean:104) bounds the halting step by n ≤ |w|^k. For k ≥ 1 and w = [] that forces n = 0, so q₀ is halting. q₀ is the same state on every input, so F never moves and f w = readTape(initConfig w, |f w|) (Reductions.lean:17), i.e. w truncated or padded with blanks. For k = 0 the machine gets at most one step, so only cell 0 can change. All of that checks out. However, nothing ties |f w| to the machine, so the output length may be any (even non-computable) function of w. Example: f w = [tape cell 0] if w ∈ A, else []. With the trivial halting F and k = 1 this is admissible, so every language A, even an undecidable one, satisfies A ≤ₚ {length-1 strings}. So ≤ₚ is degenerate in both directions: too restrictive about content and too permissive about length. IsPSPACEComplete is therefore not simply 'far stronger' than the textbook notion; it is a different and broken notion. Either way the Lean definition does not match Sipser's notion of polynomial-time reducibility, so needs-lean-change stands. The upstream issue should also require the output to be determined, e.g. f w blank-free with a blank at cell |f w|, or 'just f(w) on the tape' as in Sipser. Adding a constant to the time bound alone does not fix it. IsPSPACEComplete itself (SpaceComplexity.lean:163) matches the article's wording.

InBPP is `∃ (Q : Type) (_ : DecidableEq Q) (M : PTM Q Γ) k t', M.runsInTime t' ∧ IsBigO t' (n^k) ∧ M.decidesWithError A (1/3) t'`. It has no Fintype Q, while InTIME/InNTIME (Complexity.lean:81,86) do require one. The PTM structure doesn't require finite states either. The auditor's construction typechecks against the real fields. Take Q = ℕ ⊕ Bool, Γ = Bool, blank = false, inputAlpha = {true}, δ₀ = δ₁. State inl n reads true → inl (n+1) and moves R. On reading false it goes to qAccept if n ∈ S and to qReject otherwise. It halts within |w|+1 steps on every branch. Halting configs are fixed points in stepWithCoin, so runsInTime (n+1) holds and the error is 0. So Lean-BPP contains languages built from an arbitrary (even undecidable) S ⊆ ℕ. The second finding also holds. decidesWithError quantifies over every w : List Γ. initConfig w and initConfig (w ++ [blank]) are the same tape function, so the two runs agree. That means no nonempty finite language is in Lean-BPP (take a longest word w; then w++[blank] ∉ A). This is a material mismatch with the textbook class.

Checked SpaceConstructible (HierarchyTheorems.lean:274-278), TM, initConfig and run (TuringMachines.lean:30-84), and TMSpaceUsed, TMRunsInSpace and InSPACE (SpaceComplexity.lean:23-45). The two initial tapes are equal as functions: initConfig (replicate m M.blank) gives blank at every cell, and so does initConfig []. Since state and head position also match, the two runs are identical. M is a decider, so it halts on [] at some step n. TMSpaceUsed depends only on runOnInput, so f m = TMSpaceUsed M [] n = f 0, and f is constant, say k. TMSpaceUsed is the card of the image of the nonempty range(n+1), so k ≥ 1. The TM with q₀ = qAccept shows f ≡ 1 does satisfy the hypothesis. For constant k, IsAsympDominated g f with c = k forces g n = 0 eventually. TMRunsInSpace requires halting with space at least 1 ≤ g|w|, so for nonempty Γ no A is in InSPACEo, and the conclusion reduces to the trivial ∃ A ∈ SPACE(O(1)). For Γ = Empty no TM exists (field blank : Γ), so InSPACE fails and the statement is false. This is possible because Γ is universally quantified, independent of the alphabet in hf, and the proof goes through the sorry'd sim_overhead. Sipser's space constructibility is not captured, so this needs a Lean change.
